summary: First steel lookout tower built in New Hampshire, erected 1914 on the south knob of Mount Pawtuckaway; standing, in state park, climbable per trip reports.

facts.design: 25-foot steel tower erected in 1914; modified in 1930; raised 10 feet in 1971; new cab installed in 1976

staffing.status: in active service per the Register; no current staffing schedule in the sources read

access.note: Inside Pawtuckaway State Park. The park trail sheet promotes the fire tower view from South Mountain. Trip reports describe climbing to the top platform. No closure notice found.

visit.trail_note: Hike into Pawtuckaway State Park to the South Mountain summit. The park trail sheet gives a 2.4-mile walk to the 908-foot summit. A 2020 trip report describes three flights of steep stairs to the top platform. Check the park before visiting.

facts.agency: NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development

events.note: 25-foot steel tower erected; described as the first steel lookout tower built by the state
State bought the Goodrich property on the mountain
Tower modified; the old house on the bought property was to be occupied by the forestry watchman in fire season
New cab installed and the tower painted

corrections.why: The 2016 chapter report says a new cab was installed and the tower painted. That is repair and maintenance, not a restoration to service.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives the site elevation as 549 feet (167 m). The park trail sheet puts the fire tower on the 908-foot summit of South Mountain. The story uses the Register figure only with a caution. The brief's elevation_m 167.3 is the Register value and was left in the record.

notes_for_editor: The Register and the 1914 and 1930 items are consistent on the first steel tower, the 1971 raise and the 1976 cab. Sources do not agree on the site elevation: the Register says 549 feet, but the park sheet puts the tower on the 908-foot summit of South Mountain. The 1930 house item is a plan from a newspaper, not a confirmed use. The 1938 and 1920 items are from a Portsmouth Herald excerpt quoted on the Forest Lookouts page and not checked against the original paper. The 2016 chapter report's statewide staffing line is not specific to this tower and is not used. The OpenStreetMap way lists the operator as NH Division of Forests and Lands; the Register names NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development, so the story uses the Register. Climbing is supported only by two personal blogs and a park mention of the view; the story says to check with the park. Leads: park or NH Division of Forests and Lands notice about tower access; a 1914 Biennial Report copy for the original build detail. The 1930 notice also says the tree line was replaced by ground wire; the story does not say the Goodrich house was wired.
